subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What trust boundary and default activation policy should OpenClaw enforce for plugin, agent, or external recurring cron jobs that can spend model quota?
rationale: A mechanical fix would change public cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model spend policy, and upgrade behavior, so maintainer intent is needed before implementation.

options.title: Provenance-gated scheduling API
options.body: Require trusted origin attribution plus approval or disabled-by-default activation for non-operator recurring jobs, and require explicit model/cost policy before execution.

options.title: Default external jobs disabled
options.body: Make plugin, agent, and external recurring registrations inactive until the operator enables them, accepting a compatibility migration and UX cost for existing automation.

options.title: Keep auto-enable with spend guards
options.body: Preserve current activation behavior but add budget, quota, and cost circuit breakers, leaving consent and provenance weaker than the issue requests.

recommendation.title: Provenance-gated scheduling API
recommendation.body: Require trusted origin attribution plus approval or disabled-by-default activation for non-operator recurring jobs, and require explicit model/cost policy before execution.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron/model-selection and release history puts the active implementation surface closest to Vincent Koc, while the final policy still needs broader security/product agreement.
